newsitem.title: USA: Air Canada not surprised if Southwest competes.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada not surprised if Southwest competes.

text.p: Air Canada president Lamar Durrett said on Wednesday he would not be surprised if low-cost Southwest Airlines Co entered the Canadian market, although he saw no present signs of it.

Durrett also said the application by United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp, for antitrust immunity for a marketing link-up with Air Canada was moving along and "we have not detected any particular problems."
He told the Canadian-American Business Council that the anti-trust immunity for its tie with United would maintain a level playing field in U.S.-Canada aviation traffic.
Durrett noted that the U.S. government recently granted antitrust immnity to a link between Canadian Airlines Corp and American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp.
He said he knew of no plans for Southwest, which soon is to extend operations to the Northeast U.S., to move into Canada, but "We would not be surprised to see that happen."
Durrett added, however, that "Air Canada will not roll over if Herb crosses the border," a reference to Southwest president Herbert Kelleher.

He called the U.S.-Canada "open skies" aviation accord a success in increasing cross-border air traffic, and noted that the third-year phase of the pact begins next February when U.S. airlines will have full access to Montreal and Vancouver, along with greater access to Toronto.
Toronto opens up completely in February 1998, he said, meaning more competition, but he said "I don't see this as a particular threat to Air Canada," which has a major hub there.

He said Air Canada remained opposed to an earlier full opening of Toronto, which Canada insisted be part of the free-market air pact, to give it time to establish itself as a competitor with the many big American carriers that now serve Canada's largest city.
